questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The opportunity to study in the UK and better my English abilities academic wise. And also that the university had Africa studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly essay. There was alot to read and information to be awar off, but once you did that it was okay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There was a Fresher Start week. And you could write to the Study Abord Office, and also go to the counter service in the Student Union building if you need help and assistance. I did not use any of them.
You are also given a parent school and a personal tutor through them. That person is also their to help you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
It was okay once I reach out. But there was a strick while I was their which affacted a lot of things. 
When I was in dought with some stuff about choosing modules or other things I just email or called Study Abord Office and they put me in contact who I should speak to. Or I simpel ask the teacher/lecture of the curtain module. They were all really helpfull once you asked,

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really easy. I used the university accommodation service and lived in one of their housings.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to find a cheaper option use private accommodation services. The university recommend some you can use. And if you want to find an accommodation through private once start looking really early. They get occupied really quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process is long and you have to be patient. There is a lot to read, but otherwise it is okay.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it as fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can find most on the University of Leeds webpage. But they also send you emails of 'Preparing to Study at the University of Leeds' with to-do lists, specfic deadlines etc. so just pay attention to your email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not that successful as I was appling for some popular modules/classes outside my academic discipline. And when their is a lot of applicants they tent to choose student within the discipline.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I would give the advice if you really want specific classes to really make an effort in the motivation letter when you are doing the registering at University of Leeds. They really read it and choose you for the specific classes because of that. 
And if you do not get choosen for your first choices of classes it is okay. I only got one of the modules I originally applied for, and it ended up being my least favorite one of all 4 of my modules. (#When life gives you lemon - you make lemonade)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was at a medium, but only because I did not get the modules and type of academic programme I originally wanted.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level was fine. Once you got used to read the texts and your vocabulary got better with time the more esay was the acadmics. 
You have a lot of academic freedom; meaning due to Leeds being a part of The Russell Group Universities there is a focus on own research and independence. So my exsams was flexible enough to be about my own interest.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The lectures are not that long. And it is mostly just read at home and listen to a monolog-lecture (of cause you can ask questions) But then they have seminars were you can be more active (some seminars are of cause better then others). 
I really felt that there wasn't a fare distance for student to teacher at Leeds. Meaning the teachers had office hour each week where you could drop in if you needed advice or something. Or you chould send them an email if you were in need of help and they answar really quickly.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Religion in Modern Africa 
Sociology of Religion
Academic English
English Through Interpersonal Communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Choose want ever seems interessting and fun. And do not be afaird of the langague level you get use to it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: How much I use to travel on public transport

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The food and groceries are a bit expersive when you look at the quality of food. I choose to cook a lot to save money and not eat out as much as my friends did. 
Also the housing. It is more expersive then Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Everything! Leeds has alot of Student Social Societies. Everything from any kind of sport to any time of culturel and social soceity, music, social, teacter, non-alcohol societies ect. ect. ect.
They also have a gym on campus. And if you live around campus in a university accommodation it is for free to train there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Look at the Leeds University Union webpage and just sign up to all the Social Societies that you find interessting. It is the best way to find new friends especially British onces. And look for Student Activities and go to them. It is really the best way to get friends.

Look for GO OUT GET ACTIVE. They arrange trips and the walking onces are really fun and a good for you to go to the national parks for a day trip.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the national parks such as Yorkshire Dales and Lake District. It is fun to get a break from the city and see the mountains. 
Manchester is really close and cheap to travel to if you are interessed.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. First of all because you are just around students from everywhere. Some for a one semester exhange, some for a whole degree, some are local Britis, some are international. Second of all if is different from Denmark, but still Western Europe so not that different again.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be a memeber of Social Societies and participate in Student Activites! The more is better, especially in the start of the semester. You don't know which ones really fit you, so just turn up to alot of them in the start and then you can always be less active if you get too busy or they are not the once for you. Social Societies in Leeds don't demand alot. You just participate in the Social events the committee have arrange for the Society

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: English people talk alot, and you have to remember to answer politely all the time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open and polite English people are :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient with the registering processes at UCPH and at University of Leeds. There is alot of things to do and read etc. etc. but once you get through them it is okay. And send emails if you are in dought.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I have expressed them already.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That you really are being pussed in your English langauge skills and you really develop alot. You will be surprice at how much you actually are able to do and preform in academics.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing schools and exsams and really get on the other sides of them. And managing to have a life abord in an English speaking country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
